threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a ‘supermarket’ instead of the much cooler ‘local shop’. You’re definitely not from these parts.
Last night on the 45, heard a guy singing to himself while holding a half-eaten patty. Only in Brixton do midnight snacks come with live music.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a pigeon strutting confidently in front of a café, completely ignoring the hipsters inside, was when I knew I was one of them.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how the S-Bahn rides are punctuated by impromptu accordion players? It's like a live soundtrack to your commute, adds a twist to the daily grind.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local if they can name the last time BART had a meltdown and still give you solid gossip about the latest taco truck opening.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo looking like he just left a wedding, trying to impress a pigeon on the corner of Turk and Jones. Classic SF vibe.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think all the locals are friendly, but most of us just nod and keep walking. It's a head-down culture here, not a smile-fest.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their overzealous snapping of photos at every corner; the locals just glance and walk by the same murals.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'London Fields' is a park rather than a local vibe, and you're bewildered by the brunch queues that start before 10am.
Saw a guy on the N21 last night trying to barter his old vinyl records for a ticket. The driver just shook his head and kept driving.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of freshly baked pastries at the corner bakery and the sound of mixed languages in the park—it hits different on a sunny Saturday.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find an abandoned amusement park like Spreepark turned into a playground for urban explorers and a backdrop for film shoots. Total surrealism.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Real locals know to avoid Civic Center BART when something goes boom. Tourists just stare at the chaos, frozen like deer in headlights.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy with a dog in a sweater calmly reading a novel on the 14 Mission. Only in San Francisco do we ride the bus like it’s a café.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think all bars are full till dawn, but locals know the best vibe is at 10 PM, when the tapers are fresh and conversations are real.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll know a recent arrival by their hesitation at the metro ticket machines; they’re still sifting through the options like it’s a Rubik's cube.
